title: Stitched segmented KV allocator and batch-aware prefetch prototype
creator: Maya Patel
description: Prototype a 'stitched segmented' KV cache allocator with a batch-aware prefetcher and asynchronous GPU->host paging to reduce P99 tail latency and OOM events when serving large-context models under continuous batching. This ticket covers design, implementation of a prototype allocator + prefetch hints from the batching controller, integration with the async swap queue, and a short experiment harness to validate on 7B and 13B models.
decision: Implement a segmented allocator (variable-sized segments carved from fixed-size pages) to reduce fragmentation and allow bulk prefetch/eviction operations. Prefetch hints will be emitted by the continuous-batching controller for batch-head prefixes and long-running KV hits. Evictions will be async and use pinned host buffers + GPUDirect path where available.
tradeoffs: Segmentation reduces internal fragmentation vs fixed-slab allocators but increases allocator complexity and requires an epoch-based reclamation to avoid races with in-flight kernels. Prefetch reduces miss latency at the cost of additional memory churn and potentially wasted IO on mispredicted prefixes. Using pinned host memory + GPUDirect reduces copy overhead but complicates deployment on air-gapped/private nodes without that capability.
implementation_notes: Key pieces: (1) Page and segment metadata stored in host-pinned page table with compact bitfields for residency and pin-count; (2) Segments carved from 2MB pages, segment header contains model-id, sequence-range, quantization-flag; (3) Async eviction worker uses a prioritized queue: hot pages (recent hits) are kept, cold pages are batched for swap-out in 8MB IO units; (4) Prefetch hints are vector of segment-ids with predicted offsets and issued by batching controller when a request becomes head-of-batch or is observed in repeated sequences; (5) OOM handler first tries deferred eviction + backpressure to the batching controller to reduce concurrency, then falls back to on-the-fly compression of victim segments (4-bit quantization) before last-resort OOM failure.
metrics_and_slo_targets: Measure: page-faults per 100k tokens, eviction latency (median and P99), extra IO bytes due to prefetch, P95/P99 generation latency delta vs baseline, OOM rate. Targets: reduce OOMs by 90% under current load profile, keep P99 generation latency increase <= 10% for 13B under 750ms SLO, page-faults < 5 per 100k tokens for modeled workloads.
test_plan: (1) Unit tests for allocator invariants and epoch reclamation. (2) Microbenchmarks: synthetic access patterns (hot-cold, streaming, reverse-scans) to validate memory churn and eviction IO. (3) End-to-end: replay production traces (anon) for two cohorts: chat-heavy and long-context batch streams against llama-2-13B and mosaic-7B. (4) Fault injection: disable GPUDirect path to validate host-copy fallback and measure latency regressions.
rollout_plan: Start as a behind-feature-flag prototype on dedicated dev cluster. Run A/B with 10% traffic (low-load models) for 2 weeks. If metrics are green, expand to 25% including a canary on Dedicated SKU customers with opt-in. Provide kill-switch to disable prefetch at runtime and revert to current slab allocator. Final enablement target for runtime-1.20 if stable.
risks_and_mitigations: Race between eviction and active KV reads: mitigate with lightweight epoch counters and per-segment pin counts; require allocator tests.
Prefetch misprediction leading to extra IO: cap prefetch budget per-request and track wasted-prefetch metric; backoff on low precision.
Increased host-memory usage on nodes without GPUDirect: detect capability at startup and lower prefetch aggressiveness or fall back to on-demand transfer.
Complexity causing hard-to-debug OOMs: expose detailed residency traces in Console and add automatic snapshot on OOM for postmortem.
Performance regressions for small models: gate by model-size whitelist and runtime flags.
experiments_and_results: 2025-02-20: Microbench (hot-cold 90/10) on dev: segmented allocator reduced fragmentation by ~28% vs slab, eviction IO reduced 18%.
2025-02-25: End-to-end replay on llama-2-13B trace: P99 generation latency increased 6% with aggressive prefetch, OOMs dropped from 4/hr to 0.4/hr.
2025-02-28: GPUDirect disabled test: P99 delta increased to 18% under high-concurrency—plan to implement softer prefetch budget on such hosts.
Next: tune prefetch thresholds and implement per-model prefetch policy and a simple ML-based misprediction scorer.

Customer asks: several customers reported OOMs with long-context workflows—this prototype prioritizes reducing those incidents without large latency regressions.
Security: no customer data leaves the host; paged data remains encrypted at rest and in host memory per Private deployment requirements.
